terms.name: Why Accessibility Matters & WCAG (POUR, levels)
terms.one: Accessibility (a11y) makes products usable by people with disabilities; WCAG defines testable success criteria grouped under Perceivable, Operable, Understandable and Robust (POUR) at levels A, AA and AAA.

terms.name: Semantic HTML, Landmarks & Headings for Accessibility
terms.one: Native semantic elements give assistive technology roles, names and states for free; landmarks and a logical heading outline let screen-reader users navigate quickly.

terms.name: ARIA, Keyboard & Focus Management (WCAG 2.2)
terms.one: Make interfaces usable with keyboards and screen readers using semantic HTML first, ARIA only to fill gaps, and deliberate focus handling.

terms.name: Accessible Names & Descriptions
terms.one: Every interactive element needs an accessible name (what it is called) computed from content, labels, aria-labelledby, aria-label, alt or title; descriptions add extra context.

terms.name: Keyboard Accessibility & Focus Order
terms.one: Everything must work with a keyboard: reachable with Tab, operable with Enter/Space/arrow keys, in a logical order, with a clearly visible focus indicator and no keyboard traps.

terms.name: Focus Management in SPAs, Modals & Dynamic Content
terms.one: Move focus deliberately when UI changes: into dialogs and back to the trigger on close, to new page headings after client-side navigation, and to errors after failed submits.

terms.name: Accessible Forms & Error Handling
terms.one: Accessible forms have visible labels, grouped related fields, clear instructions, accessible error messages linked to fields and don’t rely on colour alone.

terms.name: Accessible Widget Patterns (ARIA APG): tabs, menus, combobox, modal
terms.one: The WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) defines roles, states and keyboard behaviour for custom widgets like tabs, menus, comboboxes, accordions, dialogs, tooltips and carousels.

terms.name: Live Regions & Dynamic Announcements
terms.one: ARIA live regions (aria-live, role="status", role="alert") announce dynamic content changes like toasts, form results, loading states and chat messages to screen-reader users.

terms.name: Colour Contrast & Use of Colour
terms.one: Text needs sufficient contrast with its background (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large text and UI components), and colour must never be the only way to convey information.

terms.name: Accessible Images, Icons, Video & Audio
terms.one: Provide text alternatives for images, hide decorative ones, caption videos, transcribe audio, avoid auto-playing media and give users control over motion.

terms.name: Zoom, Reflow, Target Size & Motion
terms.one: Content must work at 200% text zoom and 400% page zoom (reflow without horizontal scrolling at 320px), touch targets need adequate size (24×24px minimum, 44px recommended), and motion should respect user preferences.

terms.name: Screen Readers & Assistive Technology Testing
terms.one: Test with real assistive technology: NVDA/JAWS (Windows), VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), TalkBack (Android), plus keyboard-only, voice control and zoom.

terms.name: WCAG 2.2 Updates & Running an Accessibility Audit
terms.one: WCAG 2.2 (2023) added criteria such as Focus Not Obscured, Dragging Movements, Target Size, Consistent Help, Redundant Entry and Accessible Authentication; audits combine automated, manual and user testing.

terms.name: AI, ML, Deep Learning & Generative AI — the basics
terms.one: AI is the broad field; machine learning learns patterns from data; deep learning uses neural networks; generative AI (LLMs, image/audio models) creates new content from prompts.

terms.name: LLMs, Tokens, Context Window & Model Parameters
terms.one: A Large Language Model predicts the next token from text input; tokens, context size, temperature and max tokens shape cost, speed and output.

terms.name: Model Landscape & Choosing a Model (Gemini, Claude, GPT, Llama, Groq)
terms.one: Choose models by quality, speed, cost, context length, multimodality, tool-use support, privacy and licensing — proprietary APIs vs open-weight models hosted by providers like Groq or self-hosted.

terms.name: Prompt Engineering for Developers
terms.one: Designing system prompts, instructions, examples and output formats so a model behaves reliably inside an app.

terms.name: Context Engineering: system prompts, memory, history & token budgets
terms.one: Context engineering decides exactly what goes into the model’s context window — instructions, examples, retrieved data, conversation history, tool results and user memory — within a token budget.

terms.name: Streaming AI Responses in the UI
terms.one: Render model output token-by-token as it arrives (via SSE or a streamed fetch body) so users see answers instantly.

terms.name: Chat UI Patterns & UX for AI
terms.one: Effective AI chat UIs handle streaming, markdown/code rendering, stop/regenerate/edit, copy, citations, suggestions, feedback, errors and accessibility.

terms.name: Generative UI & Structured Outputs
terms.one: Generative UI lets models drive rich interface components (cards, charts, forms) instead of plain text, using structured outputs or tool calls mapped to your own components.

terms.name: AI SDKs for Frontend (Vercel AI SDK, provider SDKs)
terms.one: Libraries that handle streaming, chat state, tool calls and provider switching so you write less plumbing.

terms.name: Multimodal & Voice AI in the Browser (images, audio, realtime)
terms.one: Send images, audio, video and documents to multimodal models (vision Q&A, OCR, receipt parsing) and build voice experiences with speech-to-text, text-to-speech and realtime voice APIs.

terms.name: Embeddings, Vector Search & RAG
terms.one: Retrieval-Augmented Generation finds the most relevant documents using vector embeddings and adds them to the prompt so answers are grounded in your data.

terms.name: Semantic Search & AI-powered Search UX
terms.one: Semantic search finds results by meaning using embeddings (not just keywords), often combined with keyword search (hybrid) and AI-generated answer summaries with citations.

terms.name: Tool / Function Calling & Structured Outputs
terms.one: Let the model request that YOUR code runs a function (search, fetch weather, add to cart) by returning a structured call instead of text.

terms.name: AI Agents & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
terms.one: Agents are LLMs that plan and call tools in a loop to reach a goal; MCP is an open standard for connecting models to tools and data sources.

terms.name: AI Frameworks: LangChain.js, LlamaIndex.TS, Mastra & agent orchestration
terms.one: Orchestration frameworks provide building blocks for chains, RAG pipelines, agents, memory, tool integration and observability in JavaScript/TypeScript.

terms.name: Evals, Hallucinations & Grounding
terms.one: Evaluate AI features systematically with test sets and metrics, and reduce hallucinations through grounding (RAG), constraints, citations, low temperature and verification.

terms.name: Cost, Latency & Rate Limits for AI Features
terms.one: Control AI cost and speed with smaller/faster models, prompt and response limits, caching, streaming, batching, prompt caching, model routing and per-user rate limits.

terms.name: AI Security: Prompt Injection, Data Leakage & Guardrails
terms.one: Attackers hide instructions in user input or retrieved content to hijack the model; defend with isolation, validation and least privilege.

terms.name: Privacy, Compliance & Responsible AI UX
terms.one: Responsible AI features protect user data, disclose AI usage, keep humans in control, avoid harmful outputs and comply with privacy laws and provider policies.

terms.name: On-Device / Browser AI (WebGPU, Chrome Built-in AI, Transformers.js)
terms.one: Running AI models directly in the browser for privacy, offline use and zero per-request cost.

terms.name: AI Coding Assistants in the Frontend Workflow
terms.one: Use AI assistants (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini Code Assist) to scaffold, refactor, write tests and docs — while you stay responsible for correctness, security and understanding.

terms.name: AI Feature Ideas & Product Thinking for Frontend Apps
terms.one: Practical AI features that add value in frontend products — and how to scope, measure and ship them.

terms.name: What is Angular & the Angular CLI
terms.one: Angular is a full TypeScript framework by Google with components, dependency injection, routing, forms, HTTP and testing built in; the Angular CLI scaffolds, serves, builds and updates projects.

terms.name: Components: decorator, template, styles, standalone
terms.one: A component is a TypeScript class with a @Component decorator defining its selector, template, styles and imports; standalone components are the default since v19.

terms.name: Data Binding: interpolation, property, event, two-way
terms.one: Angular binds data between class and template: {{ }} interpolation, [property] binding, (event) binding and [(ngModel)]/model() two-way binding.

terms.name: Built-in Control Flow: @if, @for, @switch, @let
terms.one: Angular’s template control flow blocks (v17+) replace *ngIf/*ngFor/*ngSwitch with faster, more readable @if, @for (with required track), @switch and @let.

terms.name: Directives: attribute, structural & custom directives
terms.one: Directives add behaviour to elements: attribute directives (ngClass, ngStyle, custom highlight), structural directives (ngTemplateOutlet, custom *if-like) and component directives.

terms.name: Pipes: built-in, custom, pure vs impure, async pipe
terms.one: Pipes transform values in templates: date, currency, uppercase, percent, json, async, plus custom pipes; pure pipes run only when inputs change.

terms.name: Component Communication: input(), output(), model()
terms.one: Parents pass data with inputs and children notify parents with outputs; signal-based input(), output() and model() replace @Input/@Output decorators.

terms.name: Lifecycle Hooks
terms.one: Angular calls lifecycle hooks at key moments: ngOnChanges, ngOnInit, ngDoCheck, ngAfterContentInit/Checked, ngAfterViewInit/Checked, ngOnDestroy, plus afterNextRender/afterRender.

terms.name: Content Projection, ViewChild & Template References
terms.one: ng-content projects parent markup into a component; viewChild/contentChild query elements and components; ng-template, ng-container and ngTemplateOutlet render templates dynamically.

terms.name: Services & Business Logic
terms.one: Services are injectable classes that hold business logic, data access and shared state, keeping components focused on presentation.

terms.name: Dependency Injection & Interceptors
terms.one: Angular creates and supplies service instances for you through hierarchical injectors; interceptors hook into every HTTP request.

terms.name: Providers & Injector Hierarchy (useClass, useValue, useFactory)
terms.one: Providers tell Angular how to create a dependency (useClass, useValue, useFactory, useExisting); injectors form a hierarchy from environment/root to components.

terms.name: Angular Router: routes, params, navigation
terms.one: The Angular Router maps URL paths to components via a Routes array, renders them in <router-outlet>, and navigates with routerLink or Router.navigate.

terms.name: Route Guards & Resolvers (functional)
terms.one: Guards decide whether navigation can proceed (canActivate, canMatch, canDeactivate, canActivateChild); resolvers fetch data before a route activates.

terms.name: Lazy Loading Routes & Components
terms.one: Load feature code only when needed with loadComponent and loadChildren, and preload strategically with PreloadAllModules or custom strategies.

terms.name: Template-driven Forms (ngModel)
terms.one: Template-driven forms build the form model from directives in the template (ngModel, ngForm) — simple and quick for small forms.

terms.name: Reactive Forms (FormGroup, FormControl, FormArray, typed)
terms.one: Reactive forms define the form model in TypeScript with FormControl, FormGroup and FormArray, giving explicit, typed and testable forms.

terms.name: Form Validation: built-in, custom & async validators
terms.one: Validators check control values: built-in (required, email, min, pattern), custom sync functions returning error objects, cross-field validators and async validators for server checks.

terms.name: HttpClient: requests, typing, errors, interceptors
terms.one: HttpClient performs HTTP requests returning typed Observables; configure it with provideHttpClient(withFetch(), withInterceptors([...])).

terms.name: resource(), httpResource() & Signal-based Data Loading
terms.one: resource() and httpResource() (Angular 19–20+) load async data into signals with built-in loading, error and reload state, re-running when their signal parameters change.

terms.name: Signals, computed & effect
terms.one: Angular's fine-grained reactive primitive: a value wrapper that notifies exactly the views and computations that read it.

terms.name: computed, linkedSignal & effect best practices
terms.one: computed() derives read-only values, linkedSignal() derives a writable value that resets when its source changes, and effect() is reserved for side effects.

terms.name: RxJS Observables & Operators
terms.one: A library for composing async event streams using Observables and pipeable operators like map, switchMap and debounceTime.

terms.name: Subjects, BehaviorSubject, ReplaySubject & multicasting
terms.one: Subjects are Observables you can push values into; BehaviorSubject holds a current value, ReplaySubject replays recent values, and share/shareReplay multicast one source to many subscribers.

terms.name: Change Detection: Zone.js, OnPush & Zoneless
terms.one: Change detection syncs component state to the DOM; Default strategy checks everything after any async event (Zone.js), OnPush checks only on input/event/signal changes, and zoneless relies on signals and explicit notifications.

terms.name: Deferrable Views (@defer)
terms.one: @defer lazily loads parts of a template (and their dependencies) based on triggers like viewport, interaction, idle, hover, timer or a condition.

terms.name: NgModules vs Standalone (migration)
terms.one: Older Angular apps organise code in NgModules (declarations, imports, providers); modern apps use standalone components, functional providers and route-level lazy loading.

terms.name: State Management: NgRx Store, Effects & Signal Store
terms.one: NgRx brings Redux-style state to Angular: Store (actions, reducers, selectors), Effects for side effects, Entity for collections and the newer SignalStore for signal-based state.

terms.name: Angular SSR, Hydration & Incremental Hydration
terms.one: Angular SSR renders pages on the server (or prerenders at build time); hydration reuses the server DOM, and incremental hydration hydrates @defer blocks on triggers.

terms.name: Testing Angular: TestBed, harnesses, Jest/Vitest
terms.one: Test Angular with TestBed for components/services, component harnesses for stable UI interactions, HttpTestingController for HTTP and Playwright/Cypress for E2E.

terms.name: Angular Performance & Security
terms.one: Optimise Angular with OnPush/signals, track in @for, lazy loading, @defer, pure pipes and bundle budgets; secure it with built-in sanitisation, strict CSP and careful bypassSecurityTrust usage.

terms.name: Angular Material, CDK, Animations & i18n
terms.one: Angular Material provides accessible Material Design components, the CDK provides unstyled behaviour (overlay, drag-drop, a11y, virtual scroll), plus built-in animations and i18n tooling.

terms.name: Angular Versions, Upgrades & AngularJS Differences
terms.one: Angular ships a major version every ~6 months with an update guide and schematics; AngularJS (1.x) is a different, end-of-life framework.

terms.name: CSS Syntax & Ways to Add CSS
terms.one: A CSS rule is a selector plus a declaration block of property: value pairs; CSS can be added inline, in a <style> tag or via an external stylesheet.

terms.name: Cascade, Specificity & !important
terms.one: When rules conflict, the cascade decides the winner by origin/importance, cascade layers, specificity and finally source order.

terms.name: Inheritance: inherit, initial, unset, revert
terms.one: Some properties (color, font, line-height) inherit from the parent by default; keywords inherit, initial, unset and revert control it explicitly.

terms.name: Basic Selectors & Combinators
terms.one: Selectors target elements by type, class, id, attribute or relationship: descendant (space), child (>), adjacent sibling (+) and general sibling (~).

terms.name: Attribute Selectors
terms.one: Select elements by attribute presence or value: [attr], [attr="x"], [attr^="x"], [attr$="x"], [attr*="x"], [attr~="x"], with an i flag for case-insensitivity.

terms.name: Pseudo-classes (:hover, :focus-visible, :nth-child, :not, :is)
terms.one: Pseudo-classes select elements by state or position: :hover, :focus, :focus-visible, :active, :checked, :disabled, :first-child, :nth-child(), :not(), :is(), :where(), :empty.

terms.name: Pseudo-elements (::before, ::after, ::placeholder, ::marker)
terms.one: Pseudo-elements style a part of an element or insert generated content: ::before, ::after, ::first-line, ::first-letter, ::placeholder, ::marker, ::selection, ::backdrop.

terms.name: The Box Model & box-sizing
terms.one: Every element is a box made of content, padding, border and margin; box-sizing decides whether width includes padding and border.

terms.name: Margin Collapsing
terms.one: Adjacent vertical margins of block elements combine into a single margin equal to the larger one instead of adding up.

terms.name: CSS Units: px, em, rem, %, vw/vh, dvh, ch
terms.one: Absolute units (px) are fixed; relative units scale: em (parent font size), rem (root font size), % (parent), vw/vh (viewport), dvh/svh/lvh (dynamic mobile viewport), ch (character width).

terms.name: Colors: hex, rgb, hsl, oklch, color-mix
terms.one: CSS colours can be written as names, hex, rgb(), hsl(), and modern perceptual spaces like oklch(), with color-mix() and relative colours for derivations.

terms.name: The display Property
terms.one: display sets how an element participates in layout: block, inline, inline-block, flex, grid, none, contents, flow-root, and more.

terms.name: Overflow, Scrolling & text-overflow
terms.one: overflow controls content that does not fit: visible, hidden, clip, scroll or auto; text-overflow: ellipsis truncates single lines.

terms.name: Sizing: min/max, aspect-ratio, calc(), min(), max(), clamp()
terms.one: Intrinsic and mathematical sizing tools: min-/max-width, aspect-ratio, fit-content, calc() and the comparison functions min(), max() and clamp().

terms.name: Fonts: font-family, @font-face, font-display, variable fonts
terms.one: Control typefaces with font stacks, load custom fonts with @font-face, manage loading with font-display, and use variable fonts for many weights in one file.

terms.name: Text Styling: line-height, spacing, wrapping, alignment
terms.one: Properties that control readable text: line-height, letter-spacing, word-spacing, text-align, text-transform, text-decoration, white-space, word-break, hyphens and text-wrap.

terms.name: Positioning: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky
terms.one: position changes how an element is placed: relative (offset from itself), absolute (relative to the nearest positioned ancestor), fixed (viewport), sticky (switches to fixed within its container).

terms.name: z-index & Stacking Contexts
terms.one: z-index orders overlapping positioned elements, but only within the same stacking context; properties like opacity, transform and isolation create new contexts.

terms.name: Flexbox vs Grid
terms.one: Flexbox lays items out along ONE axis; Grid lays them out in TWO dimensions (rows and columns).

terms.name: Flexbox in Depth
terms.one: A one-dimensional layout model: a flex container distributes space among items along a main axis and aligns them on the cross axis.

terms.name: CSS Grid in Depth (tracks, areas, auto-fit, subgrid)
terms.one: A two-dimensional layout system with rows and columns: define tracks, place items by line numbers or named areas, and auto-place the rest.

terms.name: Floats & Legacy Layout (clearfix)
terms.one: float moves an element left/right so text wraps around it; once used for whole layouts, now mainly for wrapping text around images.

terms.name: Centering Techniques & Multi-column Layout
terms.one: Common ways to centre content (grid place-items, flex, margin auto, absolute + transform) and the multi-column module for newspaper-style text.

terms.name: Media Queries & Mobile-first Responsive Design
terms.one: Media queries apply styles based on viewport width, orientation, pointer type, colour scheme and more; mobile-first writes base styles for small screens and adds min-width queries.

terms.name: Container Queries & Container Units
terms.one: Container queries style a component based on the size of its container rather than the viewport, making components truly reusable.

terms.name: Fluid Layouts, Responsive Typography & Viewport Units
terms.one: Techniques for interfaces that adapt smoothly: fluid type with clamp(), intrinsic grids, responsive images, dynamic viewport units and safe-area insets.

terms.name: User Preferences: dark mode, reduced motion, contrast
terms.one: Media features that adapt UI to user settings: prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast, forced-colors and prefers-reduced-transparency.

terms.name: Backgrounds & Gradients
terms.one: background properties set colours, images, size, position and repeat; gradients (linear, radial, conic) are generated images.

terms.name: Borders, Radius, Shadows & Outlines
terms.one: border, border-radius, box-shadow, text-shadow and outline add edges, rounding, depth and focus indicators.

terms.name: Transforms (translate, scale, rotate) & 3D
terms.one: transform moves, scales, rotates or skews an element visually without affecting layout; individual properties translate, scale and rotate can be set separately.

terms.name: Transitions
terms.one: Transitions animate a property smoothly when its value changes, defined by property, duration, timing function and delay.

terms.name: Keyframe Animations
terms.one: @keyframes defines animation steps; the animation property applies them with duration, timing, delay, iteration count, direction and fill mode.

terms.name: Filters, Blend Modes, clip-path & Masks
terms.one: filter (blur, brightness, grayscale), backdrop-filter (frosted glass), mix-blend-mode, clip-path shapes and mask images create visual effects without images.

terms.name: Modern CSS: Container Queries, :has(), Nesting, Layers, View Transitions
terms.one: New native CSS features that replace many JS and preprocessor tricks.

terms.name: Custom Properties (CSS Variables) & @property
terms.one: Custom properties (--name: value) are runtime variables that cascade and inherit, readable with var() and changeable from JS; @property registers typed, animatable variables.

terms.name: Native CSS Nesting
terms.one: Write nested rules directly in CSS (like Sass): child selectors, & for the parent, and nested media/container queries.

terms.name: The :has() Relational Selector
terms.one: :has() matches an element if it contains (or is followed by) something matching the argument — the long-awaited "parent selector".

terms.name: Cascade Layers (@layer)
terms.one: @layer groups styles into ordered layers; later layers win regardless of selector specificity, making large CSS predictable.

terms.name: View Transitions API
terms.one: Animate between page states (or full page navigations) by letting the browser snapshot old and new views and cross-fade/morph them.

terms.name: Scroll Snap, Scroll-driven Animations & smooth scrolling
terms.one: Native scroll features: scroll-snap for carousels, scroll-behavior for smooth anchors, and scroll-driven animations tied to scroll position.

terms.name: Anchor Positioning
terms.one: CSS anchor positioning tethers an element (tooltip, menu) to another element (the anchor) with fallbacks when it would overflow — no JS positioning library needed.

terms.name: Logical Properties & Writing Modes
terms.one: Logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, inset-inline-start) follow text direction instead of physical left/right, so layouts adapt to RTL languages automatically.

terms.name: @supports, Feature Detection & Progressive Enhancement
terms.one: @supports applies CSS only when the browser supports a property/value or selector, enabling progressive enhancement.

terms.name: CSS Architecture: BEM, OOCSS, ITCSS, Utility-first
terms.one: Naming and organisation strategies that keep large CSS codebases maintainable: BEM (block__element--modifier), OOCSS, ITCSS layering, SMACSS and utility-first.

terms.name: Sass/SCSS & Preprocessors
terms.one: Sass (SCSS) extends CSS with variables, nesting, mixins, functions, loops and partials, compiled to plain CSS at build time.

terms.name: Scoped Styles: CSS Modules, CSS-in-JS & Framework Scoping
terms.one: Techniques to scope CSS to components: CSS Modules (hashed class names), CSS-in-JS (styled-components, Emotion, zero-runtime vanilla-extract/Panda), Angular/Vue scoped styles and Shadow DOM.

terms.name: Utility-first CSS & Tailwind
terms.one: Utility-first CSS styles elements with small single-purpose classes (flex, p-4, text-sm); Tailwind generates only the utilities you use.

terms.name: PostCSS, Autoprefixer, Lightning CSS & Resets
terms.one: Build tools that transform CSS: PostCSS plugins (autoprefixer, nesting), Lightning CSS (fast minify/prefix/lower), plus resets/normalize for consistent baselines.

terms.name: Design Tokens & Theming
terms.one: Design tokens are named design decisions (colours, spacing, radii, typography) stored centrally and exposed as CSS variables to theme entire products.

terms.name: CSS Performance: critical CSS, contain, content-visibility, will-change
terms.one: Techniques to make CSS load and render faster: inline critical CSS, avoid render-blocking, reduce reflows, and use containment and content-visibility.

terms.name: Git Basics: init, clone, add, commit, push, pull
terms.one: Git tracks changes in snapshots: working directory → staging area (add) → local repository (commit) → remote (push), and pull brings others’ changes.

terms.name: Branching, Merging, Rebasing & Conflicts
terms.one: Branches isolate work; merge combines histories with a merge commit, rebase replays commits on a new base for linear history; conflicts happen when the same lines changed in both.

terms.name: Advanced Git: stash, cherry-pick, reset vs revert, reflog, bisect
terms.one: Power tools: stash shelves changes, cherry-pick copies commits, reset moves branch pointers (rewrites history), revert creates undo commits, reflog recovers lost commits and bisect finds the commit that introduced a bug.

terms.name: Pull Requests, Code Review & Conventional Commits
terms.one: Pull requests propose changes for review, run CI and document decisions; conventional commits (feat:, fix:, chore:) standardise messages for changelogs and semantic versioning.

terms.name: Git Workflows & CI/CD for Frontend
terms.one: Branch, review and merge with Git; let a CI pipeline lint, test and build every change, and deploy previews automatically.

terms.name: GitHub Actions in Depth
terms.one: GitHub Actions runs workflows (YAML) on events like push or pull_request using jobs, steps, reusable actions, secrets, caching, matrices and environments.

terms.name: Deploying Frontends: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, static hosting
terms.one: Frontend hosting platforms build from Git, deploy to a global CDN, create preview URLs per PR and run serverless/edge functions; static sites can also go to S3+CloudFront, GitHub Pages or Firebase Hosting.

terms.name: Environments, Config & Secrets Management
terms.one: Separate development, preview/staging and production with environment-specific configuration and secrets stored in the platform — never in the repository.

terms.name: Docker for Frontend Apps
terms.one: Docker packages an app with its runtime into an image for consistent builds and deployments; frontends use multi-stage builds (Node build → nginx or Node runtime).

terms.name: Feature Flags, A/B Testing & Personalisation
terms.one: Feature flags toggle features at runtime without deploying; A/B testing randomly assigns variants and measures impact; personalisation targets content to segments (e.g. Adobe Target, Optimizely, LaunchDarkly).

terms.name: Monitoring, Error Tracking & Analytics
terms.one: Observe production frontends with error tracking (Sentry), real-user performance monitoring, logs, uptime checks, product analytics (GA4, Mixpanel, PostHog) and session replay — with privacy controls.

terms.name: Release Strategies: canary, blue-green, rollback, versioning
terms.one: Ship safely with canary releases (small % of users first), blue-green deployments (switch traffic between two environments), instant rollbacks, semantic versioning and release notes.

terms.name: What is HTML & How Browsers Render It
terms.one: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) describes the structure and meaning of web content; the browser parses it into the DOM and renders it.

terms.name: Document Structure: DOCTYPE, html, head, body
terms.one: Every HTML page has a DOCTYPE declaration, a root <html> element, a <head> for metadata and a <body> for visible content.

terms.name: Elements, Tags & Attributes
terms.one: An element is an opening tag, content and closing tag; attributes are name="value" pairs in the opening tag that configure it.

terms.name: Global Attributes (id, class, data-*, hidden, tabindex…)
terms.one: Attributes that can be used on any HTML element, such as id, class, style, title, lang, dir, hidden, tabindex, data-* and contenteditable.

terms.name: Comments & Character Entities
terms.one: Comments (<!-- -->) are ignored by the browser; entities like < &   display reserved or special characters.

terms.name: The <head>: title, meta charset & viewport
terms.one: The head holds metadata: the page title, character encoding, responsive viewport settings and links to resources.

terms.name: Headings & Paragraphs
terms.one:

terms.name: Text-level Semantics (strong, em, mark, code, time…)
terms.one: Inline elements that add meaning to text: strong (importance), em (emphasis), mark (highlight), code, kbd, abbr, time, sub/sup, small, del/ins.

terms.name: Lists: ul, ol, li, dl
terms.one: <ul> for unordered lists, <ol> for ordered/numbered lists and <dl> for term–description pairs.

terms.name: Links & Anchors (href, target, rel, download)
terms.one: The <a> element creates hyperlinks to pages, page fragments, files, email addresses or phone numbers.

terms.name: Quotes, Line Breaks & Whitespace
