terms.name: Images: img, alt, width & height
terms.one: embeds an image; alt describes it for screen readers and failed loads; width/height reserve space and prevent layout shift.

terms.name: Responsive Images: srcset, sizes & picture
terms.one: srcset/sizes let the browser pick the best-sized image for the screen; <picture> switches formats or art direction.

terms.name: figure & figcaption
terms.one: <figure> groups self-contained content (image, diagram, code, chart) with an optional <figcaption> caption.

terms.name: Audio & Video (controls, track, captions)
terms.one: <video> and <audio> embed media natively with controls, multiple sources and <track> for captions/subtitles.

terms.name: iframe & Embedding (sandbox, allow, loading)
terms.one: <iframe> embeds another HTML page; sandbox and allow attributes restrict what the embedded page can do.

terms.name: Inline SVG vs Canvas
terms.one: SVG is a vector, DOM-based graphics format; <canvas> is a pixel bitmap you draw on with JavaScript.

terms.name: Tables: thead, tbody, th, scope, caption, colspan
terms.one: Tables display tabular data in rows and columns using table, caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th and td.

terms.name: Forms: form, action, method, enctype
terms.one: <form> collects user input and submits it to a URL (action) using GET or POST (method).

terms.name: Input Types (email, number, date, range, file…)
terms.one: The type attribute changes an input’s behaviour, keyboard and validation: text, email, password, number, tel, url, search, date, time, color, range, file, checkbox, radio, hidden.

terms.name: Labels, fieldset & legend
terms.one: <label> gives a control its accessible name and bigger click target; <fieldset> + <legend> group related controls.

terms.name: select, option, optgroup, textarea & datalist
terms.one: <select> offers predefined options, <textarea> accepts multi-line text, and <datalist> suggests values for a text input.

terms.name: Buttons: submit, button, reset
terms.one: <button> triggers actions; its type decides behaviour inside forms: submit (default), button (no default) or reset.

terms.name: Native Form Validation & Constraint API
terms.one: HTML attributes like required, minlength, pattern, min/max and type validate input natively; the Constraint Validation API lets JS customise it.

terms.name: Form UX Attributes: autocomplete, inputmode, enterkeyhint, readonly vs disabled
terms.one: Attributes that make forms faster and friendlier: autocomplete tokens, inputmode, enterkeyhint, autofocus, spellcheck, readonly and disabled.

terms.name: output, progress & meter
terms.one: <progress> shows task completion, <meter> shows a measurement within a known range, and <output> shows a calculation result.

terms.name: Semantic HTML & Modern Elements
terms.one: Using elements that describe meaning (header, nav, main, article, dialog) instead of generic divs.

terms.name: Block vs Inline & Content Categories
terms.one: Block-level elements start on a new line and take full width; inline elements flow within text. HTML5 defines content categories (flow, phrasing, interactive) that decide valid nesting.

terms.name: The <dialog> Element (modals)
terms.one: <dialog> is a native modal/non-modal dialog with focus management, Escape to close, a ::backdrop and top-layer rendering.

terms.name: <details> & <summary> (native accordion)
terms.one: <details> creates a disclosure widget that toggles content open/closed; <summary> is its clickable label.

terms.name: Popover API (popover attribute)
terms.one: The popover attribute turns any element into a top-layer popup (menu, tooltip, toast) that can be toggled by a button with no JavaScript.

terms.name: <template> & <slot>
terms.one: <template> holds inert HTML that is not rendered until cloned by JS; <slot> marks insertion points inside Web Component shadow DOM.

terms.name: SEO Meta Tags: description, canonical, robots, Open Graph
terms.one: Meta and link tags that control how search engines index pages and how links look when shared on social media.

terms.name: Structured Data (JSON-LD, schema.org)
terms.one: JSON-LD scripts describe page content (article, product, FAQ, course) using schema.org vocabulary so search engines can show rich results.

terms.name: Resource Hints: preload, preconnect, prefetch, modulepreload
terms.one: <link rel> hints that tell the browser to fetch or connect early: preload (needed now), preconnect (warm a connection), prefetch (next navigation), modulepreload (JS modules).

terms.name: Script Loading: defer, async, type="module"
terms.one: defer and async download scripts without blocking HTML parsing; defer runs in order after parsing, async runs as soon as downloaded; modules are deferred by default.

terms.name: Favicons, Touch Icons & Web App Manifest Links
terms.one: Icons and manifest links that brand your site in tabs, bookmarks, home screens and installed PWAs.

terms.name: Internationalisation: lang, dir, hreflang
terms.one: Attributes and tags that make HTML work across languages and scripts: lang, dir (ltr/rtl/auto), hreflang alternates and <bdi>.

terms.name: HTML Parsing, DOM Construction & Quirks Mode
terms.one: The HTML parser is error-tolerant: it tokenises markup, builds the DOM with tree-construction rules, auto-fixes errors and may switch to quirks mode.

terms.name: Custom Elements in HTML Markup
terms.one: Custom elements (<my-widget>) are user-defined tags registered with customElements.define, usable directly in HTML.

terms.name: Valid HTML, Deprecated Elements & Best Practices
terms.one: Writing valid, semantic, accessible markup: validate with the W3C validator, avoid deprecated elements and follow a quality checklist.

terms.name: How JavaScript Runs: Engines, JIT & Runtimes
terms.one: JavaScript code is executed by an engine (V8, SpiderMonkey, JavaScriptCore) that parses, compiles (JIT) and runs it inside a runtime such as a browser or Node.js.

terms.name: Variables: var, let, const
terms.one: var is function-scoped and hoisted as undefined; let and const are block-scoped, with const preventing reassignment of the binding.

terms.name: Data Types: Primitives vs Reference Types
terms.one: JavaScript has 7 primitive types (string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, null, symbol) that are copied by value, and objects (including arrays and functions) that are handled by reference.

terms.name: Type Coercion, == vs ===, Truthy & Falsy
terms.one: JavaScript automatically converts types in some operations (coercion); === compares without conversion while == converts first.

terms.name: Operators: logical, ??, ?., spread, exponent, comma
terms.one: Arithmetic, comparison, logical (&&, ||, !), nullish coalescing (??), optional chaining (?.), logical assignment (||=, &&=, ??=), ternary and spread operators.

terms.name: Control Flow & Loops (if, switch, for, for…of, for…in)
terms.one: Conditionals (if/else, switch, ternary) choose paths; loops (for, while, do…while, for…of, for…in) repeat work; break/continue control iteration.

terms.name: Strings & Template Literals
terms.one: Strings are immutable UTF-16 text values with methods like slice, includes, split, replaceAll, padStart, trim and at; template literals add interpolation and multi-line strings.

terms.name: Numbers, Math, BigInt & Floating-point
terms.one: Numbers are 64-bit floating point (IEEE 754); use Number methods for parsing/checks, Math for calculations and BigInt for integers beyond 2^53.

terms.name: Arrays: creation, mutation & immutable updates
terms.one: Arrays are ordered lists with mutating methods (push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, sort, reverse) and non-mutating ones (slice, concat, map, filter, toSorted, with).

terms.name: Array Iteration Methods: map, filter, reduce, find, some, every
terms.one: Higher-order array methods that transform (map), select (filter), aggregate (reduce), search (find, findIndex, some, every) and flatten (flatMap) data declaratively.

terms.name: Objects: literals, properties, methods & iteration
terms.one: Objects store key–value properties; create them with literals, access with dot or bracket notation, and iterate with Object.keys/values/entries.

terms.name: Object Utilities: assign, freeze, seal, structuredClone
terms.one: Built-in helpers to copy, merge, lock and inspect objects: Object.assign, spread, Object.freeze, Object.seal, Object.preventExtensions, structuredClone, Object.groupBy.

terms.name: Destructuring, Spread & Rest
terms.one: Destructuring unpacks values from arrays/objects into variables; spread (...) expands iterables/objects; rest (...) collects remaining items.

terms.name: JSON: stringify, parse & pitfalls
terms.one: JSON is a text format for data; JSON.stringify converts values to JSON strings and JSON.parse converts them back.

terms.name: Dates: Date object, time zones & Temporal
terms.one: The Date object represents a timestamp in ms since 1970 UTC; formatting uses Intl.DateTimeFormat; the newer Temporal API fixes Date’s design problems.

terms.name: Regular Expressions
terms.one: Regular expressions are patterns for matching text, used with test, match, matchAll, replace, split and search.

terms.name: Functions: declarations, expressions, arrows & parameters
terms.one: Functions are reusable callable objects defined as declarations, expressions or arrow functions, with default, rest and destructured parameters.

terms.name: Hoisting, Scope & TDZ
terms.one: Declarations are registered before code runs; var is initialised as undefined, let/const stay in a Temporal Dead Zone until their line.

terms.name: Execution Context, Call Stack & Lexical Environment
terms.one: Every function call creates an execution context (with its variables, this and outer scope reference) pushed onto the call stack; scope lookup follows the lexical environment chain.

terms.name: Closures
terms.one: A function that remembers the variables of the scope it was created in, even after that scope has finished running.

terms.name: this, call, apply & bind
terms.one: `this` is decided by HOW a function is called; call/apply/bind let you set it explicitly.

terms.name: Higher-order Functions, Callbacks & IIFE
terms.one: Higher-order functions take or return functions; callbacks are functions passed to be called later; an IIFE runs immediately to create a private scope.

terms.name: Currying, Partial Application & Composition
terms.one: Currying turns f(a, b, c) into f(a)(b)(c); partial application pre-fills some arguments; composition chains functions so the output of one feeds the next.

terms.name: Recursion
terms.one: A recursive function calls itself on smaller inputs until it reaches a base case; ideal for trees, nested data and divide-and-conquer.

terms.name: Pure Functions, Side Effects & Immutability
terms.one: A pure function returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects; immutability means never changing existing data but creating new copies.

terms.name: Memoization & Caching Functions
terms.one: Memoization caches a function’s results by its arguments so repeated calls with the same input return instantly.

terms.name: Debounce & Throttle
terms.one: Debounce runs a function only after events STOP for N ms; throttle runs it at most once every N ms.

terms.name: Prototypes & Classes
terms.one: Objects inherit from other objects through a prototype chain; ES6 class is syntax sugar over it.

terms.name: ES6 Classes in Depth (fields, private, static, getters)
terms.one: Classes provide constructor functions with methods, public/private fields (#), static members, getters/setters and inheritance via extends/super.

terms.name: Property Descriptors, Getters & Setters
terms.one: Each property has a descriptor (value, writable, enumerable, configurable or get/set) that controls how it behaves; Object.defineProperty sets them.

terms.name: Symbols, Iterators & Generators
terms.one: Symbols are unique property keys; the iterator protocol (Symbol.iterator + next()) powers for…of and spread; generators (function*) produce iterators lazily with yield.

terms.name: Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet & WeakRef
terms.one: Map stores key–value pairs with any key type; Set stores unique values; WeakMap/WeakSet hold object keys weakly so they can be garbage-collected.

terms.name: Proxy & Reflect
terms.one: A Proxy wraps an object and intercepts operations (get, set, has, deleteProperty, apply) via traps; Reflect provides default implementations of those operations.

terms.name: OOP Principles & Design Patterns in JS
terms.one: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and composition, plus common patterns: module, singleton, factory, observer/pub-sub, strategy, decorator and adapter.

terms.name: Event Loop
terms.one: The mechanism that lets single-threaded JavaScript run async work by moving finished tasks from queues onto the call stack.

terms.name: From Callbacks to Promises
terms.one: Async work first used callbacks; promises represent a future result with chaining and centralised error handling, solving callback hell and inversion of control.

terms.name: Promises & async/await
terms.one: A Promise is an object representing a future value; async/await is syntax that lets you write promise code like synchronous code.

terms.name: Timers & Scheduling: setTimeout, setInterval, rAF, requestIdleCallback
terms.one: APIs to schedule work later: setTimeout (once), setInterval (repeat), requestAnimationFrame (before next paint), requestIdleCallback (when idle) and scheduler.postTask/yield.

terms.name: Async Patterns: parallel, sequential, race, concurrency limits
terms.one: Techniques for orchestrating multiple async operations: sequential awaits, Promise.all parallelism, race/any for timeouts, and pools to limit concurrency.

terms.name: AbortController & Cancellation
terms.one: AbortController creates a signal you pass to fetch, event listeners and your own async functions so they can be cancelled.

terms.name: Error Handling: try/catch, custom errors, global handlers
terms.one: Handle failures with try/catch/finally, throw Error subclasses with context, and catch unexpected errors globally (error and unhandledrejection events).

terms.name: DOM Selection & Manipulation
terms.one: Find elements with querySelector/querySelectorAll/getElementById and change them with textContent, classList, attributes, append, remove and replaceChildren.

terms.name: Events: listeners, options, propagation & custom events
terms.one: addEventListener registers handlers for events like click, input, submit, keydown; options (once, passive, capture, signal) control behaviour.

terms.name: Browser Object Model: window, location, history, navigator
terms.one: Browser globals beyond the DOM: window (global object, size, scroll), location (URL), history (navigation stack), navigator (device/browser info), screen and alert/confirm/prompt.

terms.name: Working with Forms in JavaScript
terms.one: Read and control forms with FormData, form.elements, input events, validation APIs and submit handling.

terms.name: ES Modules vs CommonJS, import/export & dynamic import
terms.one: ES Modules (import/export) are the standard module system with static structure, live bindings and async loading; CommonJS (require/module.exports) is Node’s legacy system.

terms.name: Strict Mode
terms.one: "use strict" opts into a safer JavaScript variant that turns silent mistakes into errors; modules and classes are strict automatically.

terms.name: Memory Management, Garbage Collection & Leaks
terms.one: JavaScript frees memory automatically via mark-and-sweep garbage collection; leaks happen when unneeded objects stay reachable.

terms.name: ES6+ Features Overview (ES2015–ES2022)
terms.one: The modern JavaScript baseline: let/const, arrows, classes, modules, template literals, destructuring, spread/rest, promises, Map/Set, symbols, iterators, async/await, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, private fields and top-level await.

terms.name: Newest ECMAScript Features (ES2023–ES2025)
terms.one: Recent additions like immutable array methods, Object.groupBy, Set methods, Promise.withResolvers, Iterator helpers and RegExp improvements.

terms.name: Writing Polyfills (bind, map, reduce, Promise.all, flat)
terms.one: A polyfill implements a missing built-in feature using existing JavaScript — a very common frontend interview exercise.

terms.name: Deep Clone & Deep Equality
terms.one: Deep clone creates a fully independent copy of nested data; deep equality compares structures recursively rather than by reference.

terms.name: Tricky Output-based Questions
terms.one: Interview puzzles that test hoisting, closures, this, coercion, event loop order and reference semantics by asking "what does this print?".

terms.name: DSA for Frontend Interviews (arrays, strings, hashing)
terms.one: Common coding-round problems for frontend roles: two pointers, sliding window, hash maps, sorting, stacks/queues, trees (DOM-like) and Big-O analysis.

terms.name: What is jQuery & Why It Still Matters
terms.one: jQuery is a small JavaScript library (2006) that simplified DOM selection, events, animation and AJAX across inconsistent old browsers.

terms.name: jQuery Selectors, Events & Migration to Vanilla JS
terms.one: jQuery wraps DOM elements in a chainable object for selection, events and AJAX; modern browsers provide native equivalents.

terms.name: Selectors & DOM Traversal
terms.one: jQuery accepts CSS selectors plus traversal methods like find, children, parent, closest, siblings, next, prev, eq, first, last, filter and not.

terms.name: DOM Manipulation: html, text, attr, prop, css, append
terms.one: Methods to read/write content and attributes: .text(), .html(), .val(), .attr(), .prop(), .css(), .addClass(), .append(), .prepend(), .before(), .after(), .remove(), .empty().

terms.name: Events: on/off, delegation, trigger & namespaces
terms.one: .on() binds handlers (directly or delegated), .off() removes them, .trigger() fires events, and namespaces (click.menu) group handlers for easy removal.

terms.name: AJAX with jQuery ($.ajax, $.get, Deferreds)
terms.one: $.ajax, $.get, $.post and $.getJSON make HTTP requests and return jqXHR objects (Deferreds) that support done/fail/always and await.

terms.name: Effects & Animations (show, fadeIn, slideToggle, animate)
terms.one: Built-in visual effects (show/hide, fadeIn/fadeOut, slideUp/slideDown/slideToggle) and .animate() for numeric CSS properties.

terms.name: Utilities & Writing Plugins ($.each, $.extend, $.fn)
terms.one: Helpers like $.each, $.map, $.extend, $.isPlainObject, $.Deferred, and the plugin pattern of adding methods to $.fn.

terms.name: Migrating from jQuery to Vanilla JS / Frameworks
terms.one: Strategies to remove jQuery: map APIs to native equivalents, migrate page by page, wrap legacy widgets, and stop adding new jQuery code.

terms.name: What Happens When You Type a URL
terms.one: The journey from URL to pixels: DNS lookup, TCP/QUIC connection, TLS handshake, HTTP request, server response, then parsing, rendering and loading sub-resources.

terms.name: HTTP Basics: requests, responses, headers, methods
terms.one: HTTP is a request–response protocol: a request has method, URL, headers and optional body; a response has status, headers and body.

terms.name: REST, fetch & HTTP Status Codes
terms.one: REST maps resources to URLs and HTTP methods; fetch is the browser API to call them; status codes tell you what happened.

terms.name: HTTP Caching: Cache-Control, ETag, 304, immutable assets
terms.one: HTTP caching lets browsers and CDNs reuse responses: Cache-Control sets freshness, ETag/Last-Modified enable revalidation (304 Not Modified), and hashed filenames allow year-long caching.

terms.name: HTTPS/TLS & HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
terms.one: HTTPS encrypts HTTP with TLS; HTTP/2 multiplexes many requests over one connection; HTTP/3 runs over QUIC (UDP) to avoid head-of-line blocking and speed up connection setup.

terms.name: CORS & Same-Origin Policy
terms.one: Browsers block cross-origin responses unless the server explicitly allows them with Access-Control-* headers.

terms.name: REST API Design: resources, pagination, filtering, errors, versioning
terms.one: Good APIs use resource-based URLs, correct methods/status codes, consistent pagination and filtering, structured errors and versioning — making frontends simpler.

terms.name: Authentication: Cookies, JWT, OAuth & Passkeys
terms.one: How the frontend proves who the user is — via session cookies, bearer tokens (JWT), OAuth/OIDC sign-in, or passwordless passkeys.

terms.name: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect & PKCE
terms.one: OAuth 2.0 lets apps get limited access tokens on a user’s behalf; OpenID Connect adds identity (ID tokens) for "Sign in with Google"; SPAs must use the Authorization Code flow with PKCE.

terms.name: HTTP Clients: fetch wrappers, Axios & interceptors
terms.one: Wrap HTTP calls in a single client (fetch wrapper or Axios) to centralise base URLs, auth headers, timeouts, error handling, retries and typing.

terms.name: File Uploads: multipart, progress, chunking, presigned URLs
terms.one: Upload files with multipart/form-data, show progress, split large files into chunks/resumable uploads, and upload directly to cloud storage with presigned URLs.

terms.name: Resilience: retries, backoff, idempotency, timeouts & offline
terms.one: Make network code robust with timeouts, retries using exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency keys for safe retries, circuit breaking and offline handling.

terms.name: GraphQL, WebSockets & Server-Sent Events
terms.one: GraphQL lets the client ask for exactly the fields it needs; WebSockets give two-way real-time messaging; SSE streams one-way server updates.

terms.name: GraphQL in Depth: queries, mutations, fragments, Apollo/urql
terms.one: GraphQL clients (Apollo, urql, Relay) send typed queries to a single endpoint, normalise and cache results, and handle mutations, fragments and subscriptions.

terms.name: Typed APIs: OpenAPI/Swagger, tRPC & gRPC-Web
terms.one: Contract-first and end-to-end typed APIs: OpenAPI describes REST APIs (docs + codegen), tRPC shares TypeScript types between server and client, gRPC-Web uses Protocol Buffers.

terms.name: Polling, Long Polling & Choosing Real-time Transport
terms.one: Polling repeatedly asks the server for updates; long polling holds the request open until data arrives; SSE and WebSockets push updates — pick based on frequency, direction and infrastructure.

terms.name: CDNs, DNS & Edge Computing
terms.one: DNS maps domains to IPs; CDNs cache content on servers near users; edge functions run code at those locations for low-latency personalisation.

terms.name: BFF (Backend for Frontend) & API Gateways
terms.one: A Backend-for-Frontend is a thin server layer owned by the frontend team that aggregates and shapes backend APIs for a specific UI; API gateways centralise routing, auth and rate limiting.

terms.name: Compression, Payload Size & Rate Limiting
terms.one: Reduce bytes with Brotli/gzip compression, smaller payloads and efficient formats, and handle rate limits (429) gracefully on the client.

terms.name: What is Next.js & Why Use It
terms.one: Next.js is a React framework that adds file-based routing, server rendering, data fetching, caching, image/font optimisation and API endpoints on top of React.

terms.name: Project Structure & Special Files
terms.one: The app/ directory maps folders to URL segments; special files (page, layout, loading, error, not-found, route, template, default) define each segment’s UI and behaviour.

terms.name: Routing & Navigation: Link, useRouter, redirect
terms.one: Navigate with <Link> (prefetching, client-side transitions), programmatically with useRouter (client) or redirect() (server), and read URL state with usePathname/useSearchParams.

terms.name: Dynamic Routes, Catch-all & generateStaticParams
terms.one: Folders in brackets create dynamic segments: [slug], catch-all [...slug] and optional catch-all [[...slug]]; generateStaticParams prebuilds known params.

terms.name: Route Groups, Parallel & Intercepting Routes
terms.one: Advanced App Router features: (groups) organise routes without changing URLs, @slots render parallel routes in one layout, and (.)intercepting routes show a route in a modal while keeping context.

terms.name: Server vs Client Components in Next.js
terms.one: In the App Router, components are Server Components by default; add "use client" for interactivity (state, effects, events, browser APIs).

terms.name: Rendering: SSR, SSG, ISR, CSR & PPR
terms.one: Strategies for WHEN and WHERE a page's HTML is produced: per request, at build time, revalidated over time, in the browser, or a mix.

terms.name: Streaming & Suspense in Next.js
terms.one: Next.js streams HTML: the shell renders immediately and slow parts arrive later through Suspense boundaries and loading.js.

terms.name: Node.js vs Edge Runtime
terms.one: Routes and middleware can run on the Node.js runtime (full APIs, default) or the Edge runtime (lightweight, globally distributed, limited APIs).

terms.name: Data Fetching in the App Router
terms.one: Fetch data directly in async Server Components with fetch or any server library; client components use TanStack Query/SWR or receive data as props.

terms.name: Caching in Next.js (data cache, full route cache, router cache, "use cache")
terms.one: Next.js layers several caches: request memoisation, the Data Cache for fetch results, the Full Route Cache for rendered output and the client Router Cache, plus the newer "use cache" directive.

terms.name: Server Actions & Route Handlers
terms.one: Server Actions are async server functions callable directly from components/forms; Route Handlers are API endpoints in the app directory.

terms.name: Forms & Mutations with Server Actions
terms.one: Handle form submissions with Server Actions plus useActionState for errors/pending state, useFormStatus for buttons and useOptimistic for instant UI.

terms.name: Route Handlers (API routes)
terms.one: route.js files export HTTP method functions (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) using Web Request/Response APIs to build API endpoints inside the app directory.

terms.name: next/image: Image Optimisation
terms.one: The <Image> component automatically resizes, converts (AVIF/WebP), lazy-loads and reserves space for images to prevent layout shift.

terms.name: next/font & next/script
terms.one: next/font self-hosts Google or local fonts with zero layout shift; next/script loads third-party scripts with strategies (beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, lazyOnload, worker).

terms.name: Metadata API, Sitemaps, Robots & OG Images
terms.one: Export metadata or generateMetadata from layouts/pages for titles and social tags; add sitemap.js, robots.js and opengraph-image files for SEO.

terms.name: Performance & Bundle Optimisation in Next.js
terms.one: Keep Next.js apps fast: minimise client components, lazy-load heavy client code with next/dynamic, analyse bundles, cache data and use streaming/PPR.

terms.name: Middleware (Proxy): auth, redirects, i18n, A/B tests
terms.one: middleware.ts (renamed proxy in newer versions) runs before a request completes, letting you rewrite, redirect, set headers/cookies or block requests.

terms.name: Authentication in Next.js (Auth.js, sessions, protection)
terms.one: Implement login with libraries like Auth.js (NextAuth), Clerk or Better Auth, store sessions in secure cookies, and protect pages, actions and route handlers.

terms.name: next.config, Environment Variables, Redirects & Headers
terms.one: next.config.js configures images, redirects, rewrites, headers, output and experimental flags; environment variables are server-only unless prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_.

terms.name: Internationalisation in the App Router
terms.one: Build multilingual Next.js apps with a [locale] segment, middleware-based locale detection, dictionaries loaded on the server and hreflang metadata.

terms.name: Deploying Next.js (Vercel, Node, static export, Docker)
terms.one: Deploy Next.js to Vercel (zero-config), any Node server (next start / output: "standalone"), containers (Docker), or as static files (output: "export") with limited features.

terms.name: Pages Router (legacy): getServerSideProps, getStaticProps, _app
terms.one: The original Next.js router: files in pages/ become routes, with getStaticProps (SSG), getStaticPaths, getServerSideProps (SSR) and API routes in pages/api.

terms.name: Turbopack, Testing & Debugging Next.js
terms.one: Turbopack is Next.js’s Rust-based bundler for fast dev and builds; test Next.js apps with Vitest/Jest + Testing Library and Playwright; debug with server logs and DevTools.

terms.name: Why Performance Matters & the RAIL Model
terms.one: Faster sites convert better, rank higher and feel better; RAIL (Response, Animation, Idle, Load) gives user-centric targets for each type of interaction.

terms.name: Core Web Vitals: LCP, INP, CLS
terms.one: Google's user-centric metrics for loading (LCP), responsiveness (INP) and visual stability (CLS).

terms.name: Tools: Lighthouse, DevTools Performance, WebPageTest, CrUX
terms.one: Lab tools (Lighthouse, DevTools Performance panel, WebPageTest) diagnose issues; field data (CrUX, PageSpeed Insights, RUM) shows real-user experience.

terms.name: Real User Monitoring (RUM) & PerformanceObserver
terms.one: RUM collects performance data from actual users (web-vitals library, PerformanceObserver, Navigation/Resource Timing) and sends it to analytics to track p75 metrics over time.

terms.name: Critical Rendering Path & Render-blocking Resources
terms.one: The critical rendering path is the minimum work to show first content: HTML → DOM, CSS → CSSOM, render tree, layout, paint; render-blocking CSS and parser-blocking JS delay it.

terms.name: Code Splitting, Lazy Loading & Tree Shaking
terms.one: Ship less JavaScript up front by splitting bundles, loading code on demand, and removing unused exports.

terms.name: Image & Media Optimisation
terms.one: Images are usually the largest bytes: use modern formats (AVIF/WebP), correct dimensions (srcset/sizes), compression, lazy loading, priority for the hero and an image CDN.

terms.name: Fonts & Third-party Scripts
terms.one: Web fonts and third-party scripts (analytics, ads, chat, A/B testing, tag managers) often dominate load cost — subset/self-host fonts and load third parties late, lazily or off the main thread.

terms.name: Caching, Compression & Delivery Strategy
terms.one: Deliver fewer bytes from closer locations: long-term caching for hashed assets, CDN edge caching, Brotli compression, HTTP/2–3, and service-worker caching for repeat visits.

terms.name: Rendering Strategy for Performance (CSR, SSR, SSG, Streaming, Islands)
terms.one: How and where HTML is produced dramatically affects load performance: static and streamed server HTML beat client-only rendering for content-heavy pages.

terms.name: Reflow, Repaint & Layout Thrashing
terms.one: Changing geometry triggers layout (reflow), visual changes trigger paint, and transform/opacity can skip both (composite only); interleaving DOM reads and writes forces repeated layouts.

terms.name: Long Tasks, Main-thread Work & Improving INP
terms.one: INP suffers when the main thread is busy: break long tasks, defer non-urgent work, yield to the browser, reduce render work and move heavy computation off-thread.

terms.name: Virtualisation, Pagination & Large Lists
terms.one: Render only what is visible: virtualise long lists/grids, paginate or infinitely load data, and use content-visibility for long documents.

terms.name: Memory Leaks & Memory Profiling
terms.one: Memory leaks in SPAs grow heap usage over time (slow, crashes on mobile); find them with heap snapshots and fix uncleaned listeners, timers, subscriptions and detached DOM.

terms.name: Smooth Animations & 60fps
terms.one: Smooth animation means each frame finishes within ~16ms: animate compositor-friendly properties, use requestAnimationFrame or CSS/WAAPI, and avoid layout during animation.

terms.name: Performance Budgets & Monitoring in CI
terms.one: Performance budgets set limits (JS KB, LCP, number of requests) that CI enforces so regressions are caught before release.

terms.name: Mobile Web Basics: viewport, touch, safe areas
terms.one: Mobile-friendly web apps need the viewport meta tag, touch-friendly targets and gestures, safe-area handling for notches and performance tuned for mid-range phones.

terms.name: Progressive Web Apps & App-Store Delivery
terms.one: Web apps that install to the home screen, work offline and can be packaged for Play Store / App Store.

terms.name: Web App Manifest in Depth
terms.one: manifest.webmanifest describes how the installed app looks and behaves: name, icons, start_url, scope, display, theme/background colours, shortcuts, screenshots and more.

terms.name: Service Worker Lifecycle & Updates
terms.one: Service workers install, wait, activate and then control pages; updates follow the same lifecycle, so apps must handle new versions gracefully.

terms.name: Caching Strategies & Workbox
terms.one: Common service-worker strategies — cache-first, network-first, stale-while-revalidate, network-only, cache-only — chosen per resource type; Workbox implements them declaratively.

terms.name: Offline-first Data & Background Sync
terms.one: Offline-first apps read/write local data (IndexedDB) first, queue changes while offline and sync with the server when connectivity returns (Background Sync or manual retry).

terms.name: Install Experience & App-like UX
terms.one: Design a respectful install flow (custom prompt after engagement, iOS instructions) and app-like UX: standalone layout, offline states, splash, gestures, haptics and fast navigation.

terms.name: Publishing to Play Store & App Store (TWA, PWABuilder, Capacitor)
terms.one: Wrap a PWA for stores: Android via Trusted Web Activity (Bubblewrap/PWABuilder) with Digital Asset Links; iOS via Capacitor (WKWebView) adding native value to pass review.

terms.name: PWA vs React Native vs Flutter vs Capacitor
terms.one: Choosing a mobile approach: PWA (web, instant updates), Capacitor/Ionic (web inside native shell), React Native/Expo (native UI with React) or Flutter (Dart, own renderer) — based on features, team skills, performance and distribution.

terms.name: Advanced PWA Capabilities (share target, file handling, badging, shortcuts)
terms.one: Modern PWAs can integrate with the OS: receive shared content (share_target), open files (file_handlers), handle links (protocol_handlers), show badges, use window controls overlay and periodic background sync.

terms.name: What is React? Declarative UI & Components
terms.one: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces from reusable components that describe what the UI should look like for a given state.

terms.name: Setting up React: Vite, frameworks & project structure
terms.one: Start React projects with a framework (Next.js, React Router v7) or a build tool (Vite); Create React App is deprecated.

terms.name: JSX
terms.one: JSX is HTML-like syntax inside JavaScript that compiles to React.createElement/jsx() calls producing React elements.

terms.name: Components & Props
terms.one: Components are functions that receive props (read-only inputs) and return JSX; props flow one way from parent to child.

terms.name: Conditional Rendering & Rendering Lists
terms.one: Render UI conditionally with if/early returns, ternaries and &&; render lists with map and a stable key per item.

terms.name: Handling Events (synthetic events)
terms.one: React event handlers are camelCase props (onClick, onChange, onSubmit) receiving a SyntheticEvent that wraps the native event consistently.

terms.name: Forms: Controlled vs Uncontrolled Inputs
terms.one: Controlled inputs keep their value in React state (value + onChange); uncontrolled inputs keep it in the DOM, read via refs or FormData.

terms.name: Styling in React
terms.one: Options for styling React: plain CSS/className, CSS Modules, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS (styled-components/Emotion), zero-runtime CSS-in-JS and inline styles.

terms.name: Composition, children & Lifting State Up
terms.one: React favours composition: build complex UIs by nesting components and passing children/slots; share state by lifting it to the closest common parent.

terms.name: useState & useEffect
terms.one: useState stores values that trigger re-renders; useEffect synchronises a component with something outside React.

terms.name: useRef: DOM refs & mutable values
terms.one: useRef returns a mutable object { current } that persists across renders without causing re-renders — used for DOM access and instance-like values.

terms.name: useContext & the Context API
terms.one: Context passes a value deep into the tree without prop drilling: createContext, a Provider (or <Context> in React 19) and useContext to read it.

terms.name: useReducer
terms.one: useReducer manages state with a reducer function (state, action) => newState — useful for complex state transitions and related values.

terms.name: useMemo, useCallback, React.memo & React Compiler
terms.one: Memoisation tools that skip expensive recalculation or re-rendering; the React Compiler can now add them automatically.

terms.name: Custom Hooks
terms.one: Custom hooks are functions starting with "use" that reuse stateful logic (state, effects, refs) across components.

terms.name: useLayoutEffect, useId, useSyncExternalStore & useImperativeHandle
terms.one: Specialised hooks: useLayoutEffect (measure before paint), useId (stable unique IDs), useSyncExternalStore (subscribe to external stores) and useImperativeHandle (expose methods via ref).

terms.name: Rules of Hooks & Purity Rules
terms.one: Hooks must be called at the top level of React functions in the same order every render; components and hooks must be pure during render.

terms.name: You Might Not Need an Effect (effect best practices)
terms.one: Effects are for synchronising with external systems; derived data, event-driven logic and state resets should not use useEffect.

terms.name: Virtual DOM, Reconciliation & Keys
terms.one: React builds a tree of elements, diffs it with the previous tree (reconciliation) and applies only the needed DOM changes.

terms.name: Component Lifecycle & Class Components
terms.one: Components mount, update and unmount; class components expose lifecycle methods (componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, componentWillUnmount) that map to effects in function components.

terms.name: Error Boundaries
terms.one: Error boundaries are class components that catch rendering errors in their child tree and show a fallback UI instead of crashing the whole app.

terms.name: Portals, Fragments & StrictMode
terms.one: Portals render children into a different DOM node (modals, tooltips); Fragments group elements without extra DOM; StrictMode surfaces bugs in development.

terms.name: Suspense, lazy & Code Splitting
terms.one: React.lazy loads components on demand and <Suspense> shows a fallback while lazy code or data (via use()/frameworks) is loading.

terms.name: Concurrent Rendering: useTransition & useDeferredValue
terms.one: Concurrent features let React prepare multiple UI versions and keep the app responsive: useTransition marks updates as non-urgent; useDeferredValue lags a value behind.

terms.name: Component Patterns: HOC, Render Props, Compound Components, Headless
terms.one: Reusable composition patterns: higher-order components, render props, compound components, controlled props and headless components (logic without UI).

terms.name: React Performance Optimisation
terms.one: Make React apps fast by measuring with the Profiler, avoiding unnecessary renders, virtualising long lists, splitting code and keeping state close to where it is used.

terms.name: SSR, Hydration & Hydration Errors
terms.one: Server-side rendering produces HTML on the server for fast first paint and SEO; hydration attaches React to that HTML in the browser.

terms.name: What’s New in React 19
terms.one: React 19 introduced Actions (useActionState, useOptimistic, useFormStatus), the use() hook, ref as a prop, <Context> as provider, document metadata, resource preloading, and stable Server Components support.

terms.name: Actions, useActionState, useOptimistic & use()
terms.one: React 19 primitives for async mutations: pending state, errors, optimistic UI and reading promises/context during render.

terms.name: React Server Components (RSC)
terms.one: Components that run only on the server, can read data directly, and send zero JavaScript to the browser.

terms.name: React Compiler
terms.one: A build-time compiler that automatically memoises components and hooks, removing most manual useMemo, useCallback and React.memo.

terms.name: Routing with React Router v7
terms.one: React Router maps URLs to components with nested routes, layouts, params, loaders/actions and navigation hooks; v7 also works as a full framework (formerly Remix).

terms.name: Data Fetching Strategies in React
terms.one: Ways to load server data: effects (manual), TanStack Query/SWR (client cache), router loaders, Server Components and the use() hook.

terms.name: Form Libraries: React Hook Form + Zod
terms.one: React Hook Form manages form state with uncontrolled inputs and minimal re-renders; Zod schemas provide typed validation via resolvers.

terms.name: React Native & Cross-platform Basics
terms.one: React Native uses React to build truly native iOS/Android apps with native components (View, Text, Image) instead of DOM elements; Expo is the recommended toolchain.

terms.name: Animation & Internationalisation in React
terms.one: Animate React UIs with CSS transitions or Motion (Framer Motion) and translate them with i18n libraries like react-i18next or FormatJS.

terms.name: Frontend Security Overview & OWASP Top 10
terms.one: Frontend security protects users and data in the browser: preventing injection (XSS), forged requests (CSRF), clickjacking, data leaks, insecure dependencies and misconfiguration — guided by the OWASP Top 10.

terms.name: Same-Origin Policy & Origins
terms.one: The same-origin policy stops scripts from one origin (scheme + host + port) reading data from another, forming the browser’s core security boundary.

terms.name: XSS & Content Security Policy
terms.one: Cross-Site Scripting injects attacker scripts into your page; CSP is a browser-enforced allow-list that limits what can run.

terms.name: Content Security Policy (CSP) in Depth
terms.one: CSP is an HTTP header that whitelists where scripts, styles, images, frames and connections may come from, drastically limiting the damage of injection bugs.

terms.name: CSRF & SameSite Cookies
terms.one: Cross-Site Request Forgery tricks a logged-in browser into sending an unwanted request; SameSite cookies and CSRF tokens prevent it.

terms.name: Clickjacking & Frame Protection
terms.one: Clickjacking tricks users into clicking hidden elements of your site loaded in an invisible iframe; prevent it with CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options.

terms.name: Open Redirects, URL & Input Validation
terms.one: Validate URLs and inputs before using them: open redirects (?next=https://evil.com) enable phishing, and javascript:/data: URLs enable XSS.

terms.name: Prototype Pollution & Unsafe JS Patterns
terms.one: Prototype pollution happens when attacker-controlled keys like __proto__ or constructor.prototype are merged into objects, modifying Object.prototype for the whole app.

terms.name: Security Headers (HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy)
terms.one: HTTP response headers that harden the browser: Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and CSP.

terms.name: Supply-chain Security: dependencies, SRI, lockfiles
terms.one: Most frontend code comes from npm packages and CDNs — secure the supply chain with lockfiles, audits, update automation, minimal dependencies and Subresource Integrity for CDN scripts.

terms.name: Secure Authentication & Session Handling in the Frontend
terms.one: Handle auth safely: HttpOnly secure cookies or in-memory short-lived tokens, refresh rotation, MFA/passkeys, logout everywhere, and never trust client-side role checks.

terms.name: Trusted Types & HTML Sanitisation
terms.one: Trusted Types (a CSP feature) forces dangerous DOM sinks like innerHTML to accept only vetted objects created by policies, eliminating most DOM-based XSS; sanitizers (DOMPurify, Sanitizer API) clean HTML.

terms.name: Secrets, Environment Variables & Privacy Compliance
terms.one: Keep secrets server-side, expose only public config, minimise personal data in the browser and follow privacy laws (GDPR, India’s DPDP Act) with consent and data minimisation.

terms.name: Types of State: local, shared, server, URL, form
terms.one: Frontend state comes in kinds — local UI state, shared client state, server/cache state, URL state and form state — and each has a best home.

terms.name: Unidirectional Data Flow & Flux Architecture
terms.one: Data flows one way: state → view → user action → update → new state; Flux/Redux formalised this with actions, a dispatcher/store and views.

terms.name: Immutability, Immer & Normalised State
terms.one: Store state immutably (new references on change) and normalise relational data into id-keyed tables to avoid duplication and deep updates.

terms.name: Context-based State (React Context + useReducer)
terms.one: Combine Context with useReducer for small/medium global state without a library; split contexts and memoise values to limit re-renders.

terms.name: Redux Core Concepts: store, actions, reducers, middleware, selectors
terms.one: Redux keeps app state in a single store updated by dispatching actions to pure reducers; middleware handles side effects and selectors read/derive data.

terms.name: Redux Toolkit vs Zustand vs Context
terms.one: Ways to share client state across components — Context for low-frequency values, Zustand for lightweight stores, Redux Toolkit for large, structured apps.

terms.name: RTK Query
terms.one: RTK Query is Redux Toolkit’s data-fetching and caching layer: define endpoints once and get generated hooks with caching, invalidation and loading states.

terms.name: Zustand
terms.one: Zustand is a tiny hook-based store: create a store with state and actions, then subscribe to slices with selectors so components re-render only when their slice changes.

terms.name: Atomic State: Jotai, Recoil & signals
terms.one: Atomic state splits global state into small independent atoms that components subscribe to individually; derived atoms compute from others.

terms.name: MobX & Observable State
terms.one: MobX makes state observable and automatically re-renders components that read it, using mutable classes with actions and computed values.

terms.name: TanStack Query (Server State)
terms.one: A library that fetches, caches, deduplicates, refetches and invalidates server data with simple hooks.

terms.name: SWR (stale-while-revalidate hooks)
terms.one: SWR by Vercel is a lightweight data-fetching hook library: return cached (stale) data immediately, revalidate in the background, then update.

terms.name: Optimistic Updates & Rollback
terms.one: Optimistic updates change the UI before the server confirms, then roll back if the request fails — making apps feel instant.

terms.name: State Machines & Statecharts (XState)
terms.one: A finite state machine models UI as explicit states and allowed transitions (idle → loading → success/error), eliminating impossible states; XState implements statecharts in JS.

terms.name: State Persistence & Cross-tab Sync
terms.one: Persist state to localStorage/IndexedDB with versioning and hydration, and sync it across tabs with the storage event or BroadcastChannel.

terms.name: Choosing a State Management Approach
terms.one: A decision guide: start local, lift when needed, use a server-cache library for API data, URL for shareable state, and add a global store only for truly global, frequently changing client state.

terms.name: How to Approach Frontend System Design (RADIO)
terms.one: A structured approach for design interviews and real projects: Requirements, Architecture, Data model, Interface (API), Optimisations — RADIO.

terms.name: Choosing Rendering & Application Architecture
terms.one: Pick rendering (CSR, SSR, SSG/ISR, streaming, islands) and app structure (SPA, MPA, micro-frontends) per page type, based on SEO, interactivity, personalisation and scale.

terms.name: Component Architecture: atomic design, container/presentational, feature folders
terms.one: Organise UI into reusable layers (atoms → molecules → organisms → templates → pages), separate data logic from presentation, and structure code by feature for scale.

terms.name: Design Systems & Component Libraries
terms.one: A design system is a shared language of tokens, components, patterns and guidelines (with code + Figma) that keeps products consistent, accessible and fast to build.

terms.name: State, Data Flow & Caching Architecture
terms.one: Design where each piece of state lives, how data flows between server and UI, and how it is cached, invalidated, persisted and synchronised in real time.

terms.name: Frontend System Design & Micro-Frontends
terms.one: Structuring large frontends: choosing rendering, data flow, component architecture, and splitting apps so independent teams can ship.

terms.name: Performance Architecture at Scale
terms.one: Bake performance into architecture: budgets, rendering strategy, code splitting, edge caching, image pipeline, virtualisation, prefetching and monitoring per release.

terms.name: Security & Privacy by Design for Frontends
terms.one: Design auth flows, data exposure, input handling and third-party usage with security and privacy from the start.

terms.name: Internationalisation & Accessibility at Scale
terms.one: Plan i18n (translations, locale formatting, RTL, routing, content workflow) and accessibility (standards, components, testing, ownership) as architecture, not afterthoughts.

terms.name: Observability, Error Handling & Resilience
terms.one: Design how the frontend fails gracefully and how teams see problems: error boundaries per area, retries, fallbacks, offline states, structured logging, tracing and alerts.

terms.name: Design a News Feed (Facebook/LinkedIn/Twitter)
terms.one: A system design case: infinite, personalised feed with posts, media, likes/comments, real-time updates and great mobile performance.

terms.name: Design an Autocomplete / Typeahead
terms.one: A frequent interview design: a search input that suggests results as you type, efficiently, accessibly and race-condition free.

terms.name: Design a Chat / Messaging App
terms.one: Real-time messaging design: conversations list, message thread with history pagination, typing indicators, delivery/read receipts, offline sending and notifications.

terms.name: Design an E-commerce Product Page & Checkout
terms.one: Design product listing/detail pages and checkout for speed, SEO, conversion, accessibility and reliability.

terms.name: Machine Coding Round: common problems & approach
terms.one: Machine coding rounds ask you to build a working UI component/app in 60–120 minutes (e.g. todo, star rating, tabs, accordion, carousel, infinite scroll, nested comments, file explorer, Kanban, OTP input, progress bar, autocomplete).

terms.name: Design a Dashboard or Collaborative Editor
terms.one: Design data-heavy dashboards (widgets, filters, real-time charts) and collaborative editors (presence, conflict-free merging with CRDTs, undo/redo).

terms.name: Why Test & Testing Strategy (pyramid, trophy)
terms.one: Tests give confidence to change code; a strategy balances fast unit tests, integration/component tests and a few end-to-end tests, plus static checks (TypeScript, ESLint).

terms.name: Unit Testing with Vitest/Jest: describe, it, expect, matchers
terms.one: Vitest (Vite-native) and Jest are test runners providing describe/it/expect, matchers, watch mode, coverage and mocking.

terms.name: Mocks, Spies, Stubs & Fake Timers
terms.one: Test doubles replace real dependencies: spies observe calls, stubs return canned values, mocks replace modules; fake timers control setTimeout/Date.

terms.name: Testing Async Code
terms.one: Test promises with async/await and resolves/rejects matchers, wait for UI updates with findBy/waitFor, and control timers and network deterministically.

terms.name: Unit, Integration & E2E Testing (Vitest, Testing Library, Playwright)
terms.one: Unit tests check functions, component/integration tests check UI behaviour like a user, E2E tests drive a real browser through full flows.

terms.name: Testing Library Queries & user-event
terms.one: Testing Library renders components and queries them like users do (getByRole, getByLabelText, getByText), with user-event simulating realistic interactions.

terms.name: Mock Service Worker (MSW) for API Mocking
terms.one: MSW intercepts network requests at the network level (service worker in the browser, interceptors in Node) so tests, Storybook and local development use realistic mocked APIs.

terms.name: Testing Hooks, Components & Framework Specifics
terms.one: Test custom hooks with renderHook, components with providers (router, store, query client), and framework specifics like Angular TestBed or Vue Test Utils.

terms.name: Snapshot & Visual Regression Testing
terms.one: Snapshot tests store serialised output and flag changes; visual regression tests compare screenshots (Playwright, Chromatic, Percy) to catch unintended UI changes.

terms.name: Accessibility Testing (axe, Testing Library, manual)
terms.one: Automate accessibility checks with axe (jest-axe, @axe-core/playwright), query by roles in tests, and complement with manual keyboard and screen-reader testing.

terms.name: End-to-End Testing with Playwright
terms.one: Playwright drives real Chromium, Firefox and WebKit to test complete user journeys with auto-waiting locators, network control, tracing and parallel runs.

terms.name: Cypress
terms.one: Cypress is an E2E and component testing tool running inside the browser with a time-travel debugger, automatic waiting and network stubbing.

terms.name: Coverage, TDD/BDD & Testing in CI
terms.one: Coverage measures executed code (not quality); TDD writes tests first (red–green–refactor); BDD describes behaviour in business language; CI runs tests on every change.

terms.name: Storybook: component development, docs & interaction tests
terms.one: Storybook renders components in isolation as "stories" for development, documentation, visual review and interaction/accessibility testing.

terms.name: Node.js for Frontend Developers (nvm, npx, scripts)
terms.one: Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser and powers frontend tooling (dev servers, bundlers, linters, tests); manage versions with nvm/fnm/Volta and run tools with npm scripts and npx.

terms.name: Package Managers: npm, pnpm, Yarn, Bun
terms.one: Package managers install dependencies from the npm registry, resolve versions and write lockfiles; pnpm uses a content-addressed store and strict node_modules, Bun is an all-in-one fast runtime/toolkit.

terms.name: package.json & Semantic Versioning
terms.one: package.json describes a project (name, scripts, dependencies, type, exports, engines); semantic versioning MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with ^ and ~ ranges controls which updates are allowed.

terms.name: Transpilers: Babel, SWC, esbuild & TypeScript
terms.one: Transpilers convert modern JS/TS/JSX into code target browsers understand; Babel is plugin-based and flexible, SWC and esbuild are Rust/Go-based and much faster.

terms.name: Bundlers: Vite vs Webpack (and Rspack, Turbopack)
terms.one: Bundlers turn your modules into optimised files for the browser; Vite uses native ESM in dev for instant start.

terms.name: Webpack Concepts: entry, output, loaders, plugins, chunks
terms.one: Webpack builds a dependency graph from entry points, transforms files with loaders, extends the build with plugins and emits chunks to an output directory.

terms.name: Building Libraries: Rollup, tsup, package exports
terms.one: Libraries are built differently from apps: output ESM (and optionally CJS), type declarations, tree-shakable modules and correct package.json exports, using Rollup, tsup, Vite library mode or unbuild.

terms.name: Source Maps, Environment Variables & Build Modes
terms.one: Source maps map minified code back to original sources for debugging; environment variables and build modes configure behaviour per environment without code changes.

terms.name: Browser Support: browserslist, Baseline & polyfills
terms.one: Decide which browsers you support (browserslist query or Baseline target) so tools transpile, prefix and polyfill only what is needed.

terms.name: ESLint (flat config, plugins, rules)
terms.one: ESLint statically analyses code to find bugs and enforce conventions; modern projects use the flat config (eslint.config.js) with plugins for TypeScript, React hooks, a11y and imports.

terms.name: Prettier, EditorConfig & VS Code Setup
terms.one: Prettier auto-formats code consistently; EditorConfig shares basic editor settings; VS Code settings/extensions make format-on-save and linting automatic for the whole team.

terms.name: Git Hooks: Husky, lint-staged & commitlint
terms.one: Git hooks run scripts at commit/push time; Husky manages them, lint-staged lints/formats only staged files, and commitlint enforces commit message conventions.

terms.name: Rust-based Toolchain: Biome, Oxc, Rolldown, Turbopack, Rspack
terms.one: A new generation of frontend tools written in Rust (and Go) dramatically speeds up linting, formatting, transpiling and bundling.

terms.name: Monorepos: workspaces, Nx, Turborepo
terms.one: A monorepo holds multiple apps and packages in one repository with shared tooling; workspaces link packages, and Nx/Turborepo add task caching, affected builds and dependency graphs.

terms.name: Module Federation & Micro-frontend Builds
terms.one: Module Federation lets separately built and deployed applications load each other’s modules at runtime, sharing dependencies like React — a common way to implement micro-frontends.

terms.name: Chrome DevTools & Debugging Mastery
terms.one: DevTools panels (Elements, Console, Sources, Network, Performance, Memory, Application, Lighthouse) plus breakpoints and framework devtools are the core debugging toolkit.

terms.name: What is TypeScript & How It Compiles
terms.one: TypeScript is a typed superset of JavaScript: you add static types, the compiler checks them, then erases them to produce plain JavaScript.

terms.name: Basic Types: primitives, arrays, tuples, any, unknown, never, void
terms.one: Core types: string, number, boolean, bigint, symbol, null, undefined, arrays (T[]), tuples ([T, U]), any (opt-out), unknown (safe unknown), void (no return) and never (impossible).

terms.name: Type Inference & Annotations
terms.one: TypeScript infers types from values and context, so you annotate mainly function parameters, public APIs and places where inference is too wide.

terms.name: Typing Functions: optional, default, rest, overloads, callbacks
terms.one: Annotate parameters and returns, mark optional params with ?, type callbacks with function types, and use overloads for multiple call signatures.

terms.name: Interfaces vs Type Aliases
terms.one: Both describe object shapes; interfaces can be extended and merged, type aliases can also represent unions, tuples, primitives and computed types.

terms.name: Union, Intersection & Literal Types
terms.one: Unions (A | B) mean "one of", intersections (A & B) mean "all of", and literal types restrict values to exact strings/numbers.

terms.name: Enums, const enums & alternatives
terms.one: Enums define named constants (numeric or string); they generate runtime objects, so many teams prefer union types or as const objects.

terms.name: Type Assertions, Non-null Assertion & satisfies
terms.one: as tells the compiler to treat a value as a type (no runtime check), ! asserts non-null, and satisfies validates a value against a type without changing its inferred type.

terms.name: Narrowing: typeof, instanceof, in, equality, truthiness
terms.one: Narrowing refines a broad type (union, unknown) to a specific one using runtime checks the compiler understands.

terms.name: Custom Type Guards & Assertion Functions
terms.one: User-defined type guards (value is T) and assertion functions (asserts value is T) let your own runtime checks narrow types.

terms.name: Discriminated Unions & Exhaustiveness (never)
terms.one: A discriminated union is a union of object types sharing a literal "tag" property; switching on the tag narrows each case, and never ensures every case is handled.

terms.name: Generics
terms.one: Type parameters that let one function, class or type work with many types while keeping full type safety.

terms.name: keyof, typeof & Indexed Access Types
terms.one: keyof T gives a union of T’s keys, typeof value captures a value’s type, and T[K] looks up the type of a property.

terms.name: Utility, Mapped & Conditional Types
terms.one: Built-in and custom type transformers (Partial, Pick, Omit, Record, ReturnType…) that derive new types from existing ones.

terms.name: Mapped Types, Conditional Types & infer
terms.one: Mapped types transform every property of a type ({ [K in keyof T]: … }); conditional types choose types with T extends U ? X : Y; infer extracts parts of types.

terms.name: Template Literal Types
terms.one: Template literal types build string types from other types using backtick syntax, combined with Uppercase, Lowercase, Capitalize and Uncapitalize.

terms.name: Branded Types, Recursive Types & Variance Basics
terms.one: Branded types add a phantom tag to prevent mixing structurally identical values (UserId vs OrderId); recursive types describe nested structures like JSON and trees.

terms.name: Classes in TypeScript: modifiers, abstract, implements
terms.one: TypeScript adds access modifiers (public, private, protected), readonly, parameter properties, abstract classes and implements to JavaScript classes.

terms.name: Decorators
terms.one: Decorators are functions applied with @ to classes, methods, accessors or fields to add metadata or wrap behaviour; Angular relies heavily on them.

terms.name: Modules, Declaration Files (.d.ts) & @types
terms.one: TypeScript uses ES modules; .d.ts files describe the types of JavaScript code, and @types packages provide types for libraries that do not ship their own.

terms.name: tsconfig.json & Strict Mode Options
terms.one: tsconfig.json configures the compiler: target, module, moduleResolution, lib, paths and strictness flags like strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

terms.name: TypeScript with React
terms.one: Typing React components: props types, children, events, hooks (useState, useRef, useReducer), context and generic components.

terms.name: TypeScript in Angular (strict templates, typed forms)
terms.one: Angular is written in TypeScript: strict mode, strict template type-checking, typed reactive forms, typed HttpClient and signal types.

terms.name: Typing APIs & Runtime Validation (Zod)
terms.one: Types are erased at runtime, so validate external data (API responses, forms, env vars, localStorage) with schema libraries like Zod and infer TS types from the schema.

terms.name: What is Vue & Project Setup (create-vue, SFC)
terms.one: Vue is a progressive JavaScript framework for building UIs with reactive data and Single-File Components (.vue files combining template, script and style).

terms.name: Template Syntax: interpolation, v-bind, v-on, v-model
terms.one: Vue templates use {{ }} for text, v-bind (:) for attributes/props, v-on (@) for events and v-model for two-way binding on inputs and components.

terms.name: Directives: v-if, v-show, v-for, key & custom directives
terms.one: Built-in directives control rendering: v-if/v-else (conditional creation), v-show (CSS toggle), v-for (lists with :key), v-html, v-once, v-memo; custom directives encapsulate DOM behaviour.

terms.name: Components: props, emits, slots
terms.one: Components receive data via props (defineProps), notify parents via events (defineEmits) and accept content via slots (default, named, scoped).

terms.name: Options API (data, methods, computed, watch)
terms.one: The original Vue API organises a component by options: data(), methods, computed, watch, props and lifecycle hooks, with this referring to the component instance.

terms.name: Composition API: ref, reactive, computed, watch
terms.one: Vue 3's function-based way to organise component logic using reactive primitives inside <script setup>.

terms.name: Lifecycle Hooks
terms.one: Hooks run at component stages: onBeforeMount, onMounted, onBeforeUpdate, onUpdated, onBeforeUnmount, onUnmounted, onErrorCaptured, plus onActivated/onDeactivated for KeepAlive.

terms.name: Reactivity in Depth: Proxy, shallowRef, toRefs, nextTick
terms.one: Vue 3 reactivity uses Proxies to track property reads (effects) and trigger updates on writes; helpers control depth and conversion.

terms.name: Composables
terms.one: Composables are functions using Composition API (ref, computed, watch, lifecycle) to encapsulate and reuse stateful logic — Vue’s equivalent of React custom hooks.

terms.name: provide / inject
terms.one: provide() makes a value available to all descendants and inject() reads it, avoiding prop drilling for themes, config and services.

terms.name: Vue Router
terms.one: Vue Router maps URLs to components with nested routes, dynamic params, navigation guards and lazy loading.

terms.name: Pinia State Management
terms.one: Pinia is Vue’s official store: define stores with state, getters and actions (or setup syntax), with devtools, TypeScript support and SSR.

terms.name: Built-in Components: Transition, KeepAlive, Teleport, Suspense
terms.one: Vue ships components for animations (Transition, TransitionGroup), caching component state (KeepAlive), rendering elsewhere in the DOM (Teleport) and async loading states (Suspense).

terms.name: Nuxt: SSR, file routing & data fetching
terms.one: Nuxt is the full-stack Vue framework with file-based routing, SSR/SSG/hybrid rendering, auto-imports, server API routes (Nitro) and data fetching composables.

terms.name: Testing & TypeScript in Vue
terms.one: Test Vue components with Vitest + Vue Test Utils or Testing Library, E2E with Playwright/Cypress, and use TypeScript with <script setup lang="ts"> and vue-tsc.

terms.name: The DOM Tree, Nodes & Traversal
terms.one: The DOM represents the document as a tree of nodes (elements, text, comments); you traverse it with parent/child/sibling properties and query it with selectors.

terms.name: Event Bubbling, Capturing & Delegation
terms.one: Events travel down (capture) and up (bubble) the DOM; delegation uses one parent listener to handle many children.

terms.name: Custom Events & EventTarget
terms.one: Create your own events with new CustomEvent(name, { detail, bubbles }) and dispatch them; extend EventTarget to build event-emitting classes without libraries.

terms.name: Web Components & Shadow DOM
terms.one: Web Components are native reusable elements built from Custom Elements, Shadow DOM (encapsulated DOM and styles) and templates/slots — usable in any framework.

terms.name: localStorage & sessionStorage
terms.one: Synchronous key–value string storage per origin: localStorage persists until cleared, sessionStorage lasts for the tab session.

terms.name: Cookies from the Frontend Perspective
terms.one: Cookies are small name=value pairs the browser stores and automatically sends with matching requests, controlled by attributes like HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain, Path and Max-Age.

terms.name: IndexedDB
terms.one: IndexedDB is an asynchronous, transactional, client-side database for large structured data (objects, blobs) with indexes — the storage behind offline-first apps.

terms.name: Cache API & Storage Quotas
terms.one: The Cache API stores Request/Response pairs (used by service workers for offline assets); navigator.storage.estimate() reports usage and quota.

terms.name: IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver & MutationObserver
terms.one: Efficient browser APIs that notify you when elements enter the viewport, change size, or change in the DOM.

terms.name: Web Workers & Service Workers
terms.one: Web Workers run JS on a background thread; Service Workers sit between your app and the network for caching, offline and push.

terms.name: postMessage, MessageChannel & BroadcastChannel
terms.one: Cross-context messaging APIs: window.postMessage (frames/popups), MessageChannel (private two-way ports), BroadcastChannel (all same-origin tabs/workers).

terms.name: WebAssembly (Wasm) for Frontend
terms.one: WebAssembly is a fast, portable binary format that runs alongside JavaScript in the browser — used for heavy computation like image/video processing, games, CAD and AI inference.

terms.name: Canvas 2D, WebGL & WebGPU
terms.one: Canvas 2D draws shapes/images/text with an immediate-mode API; WebGL and WebGPU use the GPU for 3D graphics and compute.

terms.name: Camera, Microphone & Screen (getUserMedia, MediaRecorder)
terms.one: navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia accesses camera/mic streams, getDisplayMedia captures the screen, and MediaRecorder records streams to files.

terms.name: Web Audio & Web Speech APIs
terms.one: Web Audio processes and synthesises sound with audio nodes; the Web Speech API provides speech recognition (speech-to-text) and speech synthesis (text-to-speech).

terms.name: WebRTC (real-time audio/video/data)
terms.one: WebRTC enables peer-to-peer audio, video and data channels between browsers with low latency, using signalling, ICE (STUN/TURN) and encrypted media.

terms.name: Geolocation & Device Sensors
terms.one: navigator.geolocation gives the user’s location with permission; device APIs expose orientation, motion, vibration, battery and more (support varies).

terms.name: Notifications & Push API
terms.one: The Notifications API shows system notifications; the Push API with a service worker receives server-sent push messages even when the site isn’t open.

terms.name: Clipboard, Web Share, File & Drag-and-Drop APIs
terms.one: Async Clipboard API copies/pastes text and images, Web Share opens the native share sheet, File/Blob/FileReader read user files, and drag-and-drop/File System Access handle file workflows.

terms.name: History API, Navigation API, URL & URLSearchParams
terms.one: APIs for SPA navigation and URL handling: history.pushState/replaceState + popstate, the newer Navigation API, and URL/URLSearchParams for parsing and building URLs.

terms.name: Page Visibility, Lifecycle & Fullscreen/PiP APIs
terms.one: Detect when the page is hidden/shown (visibilitychange), frozen or restored from bfcache (pageshow/pagehide), and control fullscreen and picture-in-picture.

terms.name: WebAuthn & Passkeys
terms.one: WebAuthn lets users sign in with public-key credentials (passkeys) unlocked by biometrics or device PIN — phishing-resistant, passwordless authentication.

terms.name: Permissions API & Project Fugu Capabilities
terms.one: The Permissions API queries permission states; Project Fugu added powerful capabilities like File System Access, Web Bluetooth/USB/Serial/HID, Badging, Contact Picker, Idle Detection and Window Controls Overlay.
